No, the linear span of $\{\cos nt\}_{n=0}^{\infty}$ cannot approximate any nonzero odd function in $L^2((-\pi,\pi))$.

**Proof.**

Recall that $L^2((-\pi,\pi))$ decomposes as an orthogonal direct sum
$$L^2((-\pi,\pi)) = L^2_{\text{even}} \oplus L^2_{\text{odd}},$$
where $L^2_{\text{even}} = \{f : f(-t)=f(t)\text{ a.e.}\}$ and $L^2_{\text{odd}} = \{f : f(-t)=-f(t)\text{ a.e.}\}$. These two subspaces are orthogonal: for $f\in L^2_{\text{odd}}$ and $g\in L^2_{\text{even}}$,
$$\langle f,g\rangle = \int_{-\pi}^{\pi} f(t)\overline{g(t)}\,dt = \int_{-\pi}^{0} f(t)\overline{g(t)}\,dt + \int_{0}^{\pi} f(t)\overline{g(t)}\,dt.$$
Substituting $t\mapsto -t$ in the first integral and using $f(-t)=-f(t)$, $g(-t)=g(t)$ gives $-\int_{0}^{\pi} f(t)\overline{g(t)}\,dt$, which cancels the second integral. Hence $\langle f,g\rangle = 0$.

Each $\cos(nt)$ is an even function, so every finite linear combination $p(t)=\sum_{n=0}^{N} a_n \cos(nt)$ is even, i.e. belongs to $L^2_{\text{even}}$. Therefore the linear span $V=\operatorname{span}\{\cos nt : n\ge 0\}\subseteq L^2_{\text{even}}$, and its $L^2$-closure $\overline{V}\subseteq L^2_{\text{even}}$ (since $L^2_{\text{even}}$ is closed, being the orthogonal complement of $L^2_{\text{odd}}$).

Now let $f\in L^2_{\text{odd}}$ be nonzero, and let $p\in V$. By orthogonality of $L^2_{\text{odd}}$ and $L^2_{\text{even}}$,
$$\|f-p\|^2 = \|f\|^2 + \|p\|^2 \ge \|f\|^2 > 0.$$
Thus $\inf_{p\in V}\|f-p\|\ge \|f\|>0$, so $f\notin\overline{V}$. In particular, $f$ cannot be approximated arbitrarily well by elements of $V$.

Since there exist nonzero odd functions in $L^2((-\pi,\pi))$ (e.g. $f(t)=t$, or $f(t)=\sin t$), the span of $\{\cos nt\}_{n=0}^{\infty}$ cannot approximate arbitrary odd functions. In fact it cannot approximate *any* nonzero odd function; the only odd function it can approximate is $f\equiv 0$.

### PROOF COMPLETE
